payload.title: settleClaim's revisionDriftIsSelfCaused (src/state/store.mjs:1043) fails closed on legitimate…
payload.description:
settleClaim's revisionDriftIsSelfCaused (src/state/store.mjs:1043) fails closed on legitimate same-writer events that omit payload.writer, and there is no CLI verb to release an orphaned runtime claim file

Two related gaps hit live 2026-08-26 while recovering tsk-4jo from the tsk-1ck/tsk-46v class of incident (main-checkout-reset discarding an in-flight item's uncommitted events.jsonl history):

1. After tsk-4jo's event-log history was wiped and the id was re-submitted fresh under the SAME id, fgos return refused with 'settleClaim: item tsk-4jo durable revision changed from ... to ...'. The stale .fgos/runtime/claims/tsk-4jo.json (a gitignored runtime overlay file, survives git reset --hard since it is untracked) still carried the OLD preClaimRevision from before the wipe. settleClaim's own self-heal path (revisionDriftIsSelfCaused, store.mjs:1043-1071) exists exactly for 'the same writer caused this drift, reconcile it' -- but it fails closed the moment it hits ANY in-window event whose payload.writer is undefined, treating a MISSING writer field as a DIFFERENT writer (event.payload?.writer?.id !== claim.writerId is true when the left side is undefined). Confirmed live: this session's own work.add/decision/work.discovery/work.gate-approve events for tsk-4jo all omit payload.writer entirely (only work.edit/work.stage events populate it), so the self-heal check returned false on the very first event it examined, even though every single event in the window was genuinely written by the same session/writer.

2. There is no CLI verb to release/clear a single orphaned runtime claim (.fgos/runtime/claims/<id>.json) once it is in this state -- fgos pick/take refuse with 'already claimed', and the reclaim-eligibility path (isReclaimEligible, claim-liveness.mjs) is gated on an activity-staleness threshold (~24h for a session-role claim) that a just-orphaned claim will not clear for a very long time. Recovery required manually deleting the one gitignored claim file directly (rm .fgos/runtime/claims/tsk-4jo.json), which worked (readClaim treats ENOENT as the normal 'no active claim' state) but is a workaround, not a supported path -- and easy to get wrong for a caller less certain the claim is genuinely their own orphan and not another session's live work.

Suggested directions (not prescriptive): (a) make payload.writer a required, always-populated field on every event type this reconciliation logic reads (work.add/decision/work.discovery/work.gate-approve currently omit it while work.edit/work.stage populate it -- an inconsistency across verbs, not an intentional two-tier design as far as this report's evidence shows), or make revisionDriftIsSelfCaused itself skip/ignore events with no writer field instead of failing closed on them, if that omission is intentional for those event types; (b) add a CLI verb (or an explicit flag on pick/take) to release a specific orphaned runtime claim after some real, callable verification that it is genuinely stale (not just a raw rm) -- fgos-unlock's own pattern (verify liveness, refuse and report holder identity if genuinely live) is the right shape to reuse, currently scoped only to main-checkout.lock, not to a single item's runtime claim file.
